'''Sera Brodie Markoff''' (born 6 July 1971) is an American [[astrophysicist]] and is the [[Plumian Professor of Astronomy and Experimental Philosophy]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]. She is a member of the [[Event Horizon Telescope]] team that produced the first image of a [[black hole]].<ref name="eventhorizontelescope">{{cite web|url=https://eventhorizontelescope.org/organization|title=Organization|website=[[Event Horizon Telescope]]}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Sera Markoff studied physics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and was awarded a Bachelor's of Science in Physics in 1993. In 1996 she gained a Master of Arts from the [[University of Arizona]] in theoretical astrophysics, and in 2000 she gained a PhD in the same field. She was an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] Research Fellow at the [[Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy]] in [[Bonn]] from 2000 to 2002 and a National Science Foundation Astronomy & Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 2002 to 2005. In 2006 she joined the University of Amsterdam as an assistant professor, and was promoted to associate professor in 2008 and to professor in 2017.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae">{{cite web |url=https://www.seramarkoff.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/cv_new.pdf |accessdate=13 April 2019 |title=Curriculum Vitae}}</ref> From 2015 she was a full professor of theoretical [[High-energy astronomy|high energy astrophysics]] at the [[Anton Pannekoek Institute for Astronomy]], [[University of Amsterdam]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/dr-sera-markoff/1163621|title=Dr. Sera Markoff - AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|access-date=2019-04-13|archive-date=2019-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413155347/http://www.academia-net.org/profil/dr-sera-markoff/1163621|url-status=dead}}</ref> until her appointment as Plumian Professor of Astronomy and Experimental Philosophy at the University of Cambridge in December 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bothwell |first=Matthew |date=2025-12-08 |title=Professor Sera Markoff appointed Plumian Professor of Astronomy and Experimental Philosophy at University of Cambridge |url=https://www.ast.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-sera-markoff-appointed-plumian-professor-astronomy-and-experimental-philosophy |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=www.ast.cam.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>  

In 2019 she became editor of the journal ''[[Astroparticle Physics (journal)|Astroparticle Physics]]''.<ref name="Astroparticle Physics Journal">{{cite web |title=New Editors for Astroparticle Physics |url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/astroparticle-physics/news/new-editors-for-astroparticle-physics |accessdate=13 April 2019}}</ref>

== Research ==
Sera Markoff's research focuses on the interface between [[astrophysics]] and [[particle physics]], in particular problems relating to processes occurring around dense objects such as black holes. She is a member of a number of large scale research projects including the Low-Frequency ARay ([[Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR)|LOFAR]]),<ref name="Curriculum Vitae" /> [[Cherenkov Telescope Array]]<ref name="Curriculum Vitae" /> and [[Event Horizon Telescope]], which produced the first image of a [[black hole]].<ref>{{cite web |title=First-ever picture of a black hole unveiled |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/2019/04/first-picture-black-hole-revealed-m87-event-horizon-telescope-astrophysics/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410221300/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/2019/04/first-picture-black-hole-revealed-m87-event-horizon-telescope-astrophysics/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 10, 2019 |website=National Geographic |date=10 April 2019}}</ref> She is a member of the leadership of the Event Horizon Telescope project where she serves as a member of the science council and as one of the working group coordinators.<ref name="eventhorizontelescope" />

* Membership of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] 2024<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/leden/markoff |title=Sera Markoff |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |access-date=25 December 2025}}</ref>
* Willem de Graaff Prize (''Willem de Graaffprijs'') for Public Outreach, the Royal Netherlands Astronomical Society 2019<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kna-rnas.nl/willem-de-graaff-prize |title=Willem de Graaff Prize | website=Royal Netherlands Astronomical Society/Koninklijke Nederlandse Astronomenclub (kna-rnas.nl)}}</ref>

* Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] 2014<ref>{{cite web |last1=Amsterdam |first1=Universiteit van |title=Astronomer Sera Markoff appointed Fellow of the American Physical Society - University of Amsterdam |url=https://www.uva.nl/en/shared-content/faculteiten/en/faculteit-der-natuurwetenschappen-wiskunde-en-informatica/news/2015/01/astronomer-sera-markoff-appointed-fellow-of-the-american-physical-society.html |website=www.uva.nl |language=en |date=1 August 2015}}</ref>
* VICI Award 2015<ref>{{cite web |title=Vici awards 2015 |url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/Talent+Scheme/awards/vici+awards/vici+awards+2015 |website=www.nwo.nl |accessdate=13 April 2019 |archive-date=13 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413162013/https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/Talent%2BScheme/awards/vici%2Bawards/vici%2Bawards%2B2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* VIDI Personal Career Award 2007<ref name="Curriculum Vitae" />
